first: चौ॰ – राम चरित चिन्तामनि चारू। सन्त सुमति तिय सुभग सिंगारू॥
en: Rama's story is a lovely wish-fulfilling gem and a fine ornament for the lady Good Sense of the saints; Rama's many virtues are a blessing to the world and give freedom, wealth, duty and the Lord's own home.

first: सदगुरु ज्ञान बिरोग-जोग के। बिबुध बैद भव भीम रोग के।
en: They are a true teacher of knowledge, detachment and yoga, and the divine healer for the terrible disease of worldly life; they are mother and father of love for Sita and Rama, and the seed of all vows, duties and rules.

first: समन पाप सन्ताप सोक के। प्रिय पालक परलोक लोक के॥
en: They end sin, suffering and sorrow, and lovingly care for us in this world and the next; they are the brave minister of King Wisdom, and Agastya to drink up the endless ocean of greed.

first: काम-कोह कलिमल करि गन के। केहरि सावक जन मन बन के॥
en: They are a lion cub in the forest of the devotee's mind, against the herd of elephants that are lust, anger and the sins of the age; they are an honoured guest dearest to Shiva, and a rain cloud that puts out the forest fire of poverty.

first: मन्त्र महा मनि बिषय ब्याल के। मेटत कठिन कुअङ्क भाल के॥
en: They are a great charm and snake-jewel against the serpent of sense pleasures, and wipe out the hard bad lines written on one's brow; like the sun's rays they remove the darkness of delusion, and like clouds they nourish the rice crop of devotees.

first: अभिमत दानि देवतरु बर से। सेवत सुलभ सुखद हरि हर से॥
en: They give what one wishes like the best wish-giving tree, and like Hari and Hara they are easy to serve and give joy; they are like stars in the autumn sky of a good poet's mind, and like life's treasure to Rama's devotees.

first: सकल सुकृत फल भूरि भोग से। जग हित निरुपधि साधु लोग से॥
en: They are like the rich enjoyment that is the fruit of all good deeds, and like saints who do good to the world without any selfish aim; they are like swans on the Manas lake of the devotee's mind, and like the holy waves of the Ganga.

first: दो॰ – कुपथ कुतर्क कुचाल कलि, कपट दम्भ पाखंड।
en: For the fuel of wrong paths, false arguments, bad conduct, strife, deceit, pride and hypocrisy, the virtues of Rama are like a blazing fire.

first: रामचरित राकेस कर, सरिस सुखद सब काहु।
en: Rama's story, like the rays of the full moon, gives joy to all, but it does special good and great gain to the lily-like and chakor-like hearts of the good.

first: चौ॰ – कीन्ह प्रस्न जेहि भाँति भवानी। जेहि विधि सङ्कर कहा बखानी॥
en: How Bhavani asked her question and how Shankar explained it, all of that I will sing and tell, weaving it into a wonderful story.

first: जेहि यह कथा सुनी नहिं होई। जनि आचरज करइ सुनि सोई॥
en: Let no one who has not heard this story be surprised when he hears it; the wise who hear this wonderful story are not surprised, knowing this:

first: राम कथाकै मिति जग नाहीँ। अस प्रतीति तिन्ह के मन माहीँ॥
en: they firmly believe that Rama's story has no limit in the world; Rama has come down in many ways, and there are a hundred crore endless Ramayanas.

first: कपल भेद हरिचरित सुहाये। भाँति अनेक मुनीसन्ह गाये॥
en: Great sages have sung Hari's lovely deeds in many ways, differing from one world-age to another; keeping this in mind, do not doubt, but hear the story with respect and love.

first: दो॰ – राम अनन्त अनन्त गुन, अमित कथा विस्तार।
en: Rama is endless, his virtues are endless, and his story is boundless; those whose thinking is pure will not be surprised on hearing it.

first: चौ॰ – यहि बिधि सब संसय करि दूरी। सिर धरि गुरु पद पङ्कज धूरी॥
en: Having removed all doubts in this way, and placing the dust of the Guru's lotus feet on my head, I again bow to all with joined hands, so that no fault may touch me as I tell the story.

first: सादर सिवहि नाइ अब माथा। बरनउँ बिसद राम गुन गाथा॥
en: Now, bowing my head with respect to Shiva, I tell the pure tale of Rama's virtues; in the year 1631 (Samvat), placing my head at Hari's feet, I begin the story.

first: नौमी भौमबार मधु मासा। अवधपुरी यह चरित प्रकासा॥
en: On the ninth day, a Tuesday, in the month of Chaitra, this story came to light in Ayodhya; on that day, which the Vedas sing as Rama's birthday, all the holy places come there.

first: असुर नाग खग नर मुनि देवा। आइ करहिँ रघुनायक सेवा॥
en: Demons, serpents, birds, men, sages and gods come and serve Raghunayak; the wise hold a great birthday festival and sing Rama's lovely fame.

first: दो॰ – मज्जहिँ सज्जन बृन्द बहु, पावन सरजू नीर।
en: Many crowds of good people bathe in the holy water of the Sarayu, and holding in their hearts the image of Rama's lovely dark body, they repeat his name.

first: चौ॰ – दरस परस मज्जन अरु पाना। हरई पाप कह बेद पुराना॥
en: The Vedas and Puranas say that seeing, touching, bathing in and drinking its water removes sin; the glory of this holy river is so great that even pure-minded Saraswati cannot tell it.

first: राम धामदा पुरी सुहावनि। लोक समस्त विदित अति पावनि॥
en: This lovely city gives Rama's own home; it is known in all worlds as most holy. Of the countless beings of the four kinds of birth, whoever leaves the body in Ayodhya is not born again.

first: सब बिधि पुरी मनोहर जानी। सकल सिद्धि प्रद मङ्गल खानी॥
en: Knowing the city to be lovely in every way, giving all powers and a mine of blessing, I began this pure story, on hearing which lust, pride and hypocrisy are destroyed.

first: रामचरितमानस एहि नामा। सुनत स्रवन पाइय बिस्रामा॥
en: Its name is Ramcharitmanas, the Lake of Rama's Deeds; the ears find rest on hearing it. The elephant of the mind, burning in the forest fire of sense pleasures, becomes happy if it falls into this lake.

first: रामचरितमानस मुनि भावन। बिरचेउ सम्भु सुहावन पावन॥
en: Shambhu made the Ramcharitmanas, dear to sages, lovely and holy; it destroys the three kinds of faults, sorrow and poverty, and ends the bad ways and sins of the Kali age.

first: रचि महेस निज मानस राखा। पाइ सुसमउ सिवा सन भाखा॥
en: Mahesh made it and kept it in his own mind (manas), and at a good time he told it to Shiva's wife; so, looking into his heart, Hara gladly gave it the fine name Ramcharitmanas.

first: कहउँ कथा सोइ सुखद सुहाई। सादर सुनहु सजन मन लाई॥७॥
en: That same lovely and joyful story I tell; good people, listen with respect and attention.

first: दो॰ – जस मानस जेहि बिधि भयउ, जग प्रचार जेहि हेतु॥
en: Now, remembering Uma and Shiva, I tell all about what this Manas is like, how it came to be, and why it spread in the world.

first: चौ॰ – सम्भु प्रसाद सुमतिहिय हुलसी। रानचरितमानस कबि तुलसी॥
en: By Shambhu's grace a good mind blossomed in the heart, and Tulsi became the poet of the Ramcharitmanas; he makes it lovely as far as his mind allows; good people, listen with care and correct it.

first: सुमति भूमि थल हृदय अगाधू। बेद पुरान उदधि घन साधू॥
en: A good mind is the land, the heart is the deep hollow, the Vedas and Puranas are the ocean, and the saints are the clouds that rain down the fine water of Rama's fame, sweet, lovely and full of blessing.

first: लीला सगुन जो कहहिँ बखानी। सोइ स्वच्छता करई मलहानी॥
en: The play of the Lord with form, which they tell, is the clearness of that water that washes away dirt; loving devotion, which cannot be described, is its sweetness and coolness.

first: सो जल सुकृत-सालि हित होई। रामभगत जन जीवन साई॥
en: That water is good for the rice crop of good deeds and is the very life of Rama's devotees; this holy water, falling on the ground of the intellect, gathers and flows along the lovely channel of the ears,

first: भरेउ सुमानस सुथल थिराना। सुखद सीत रुचि चारु चिराना॥५॥
en: fills the fine lake of the heart and settles there; growing old, it becomes pleasant, cool, tasty and lovely.

first: दो॰ – सुठि सुन्दर सम्बाद बर, बिरचे बुद्धि बिचारि।
en: The four very lovely dialogues, made with careful thought, are the four fine landing steps of this holy and beautiful lake.

first: चौ॰ – सप्त प्रबन्ध सुजग सोपाना। ज्ञान-नयन निरखत मन माना॥
en: The seven books are its fine flights of steps, which please the mind when seen with the eye of wisdom; the boundless glory of Raghupati, beyond qualities, which I will tell, is the depth of its fine water.

first: राम-सीय जस सलिल सुधासम। उपमा बीचि बिलास मनोरम॥
en: The fame of Rama and Sita is its nectar-like water; the comparisons are the lovely play of its waves; the fine chaupai verses are its thick lotus leaves, and the clever turns of thought are the lovely pearl oysters.

first: छन्द सोरठा सुन्दर दोहा। सोइ बहु रङ्ग कमल कुल सोहा॥
en: The chhand, soratha and fine doha verses are the many-coloured lotuses that adorn it; the matchless meaning, fine feeling and good language are the pollen, honey and sweet scent.

first: सुकृत पुज मञ्जुल अलिमाला। ज्ञान बिराग बिचार मराला॥
en: Heaps of good deeds are the lovely swarms of bees; knowledge, detachment and thought are the swans; the hidden meanings, turns of speech and qualities of poetry are its many kinds of lovely fish.

first: अरथ धरम कमादिक चारों। कहब ज्ञान बिज्ञान बिचारी॥
en: The four goals of life, wealth, duty, desire and freedom, and the discussion of knowledge and wisdom, the nine tastes of poetry, prayer, penance, yoga and detachment, are all the fine water creatures of this lake.

first: सुकृती साधु नाम गुन गानो। ते बिचित्र जल बिहँग समाना॥
en: The singing of the names and virtues of holy and good people is like the many kinds of water birds; the gatherings of saints are the mango groves all around, and faith is said to be the spring.

first: भगति निरूपन बिबिध बिधाना। छमा दया दम लता बिताना॥
en: The many ways of describing devotion, with forgiveness, kindness and self-control, are the bowers of creepers; calm, restraint and discipline are the flowers, wisdom is the fruit, and love for Hari's feet is the juice, as the Vedas say.

first: औरउ कथा अनेक प्रसङ्गा। तेइ सुक पिक बहु बरन विहङ्गा॥८॥
en: And the many other stories and episodes in it are the parrots, cuckoos and birds of many colours.

first: दो॰ – पुलक बाटिका-बाग बन, सुख सुविहङ्गविहारु।
en: The thrill of joy is the gardens, groves and forests, and happiness is the play of the birds; a good mind is the gardener who waters them with the water of love from the lovely pots of the eyes.

first: चौ॰ – जे गावहिं यह चरित सँभारे। तेइ एहि ताल चतुर रखवारे॥
en: Those who sing this story with care are the skilled guards of this lake; the men and women who always hear it with respect are the fine gods who have a right to this Manas.

first: अति-खल जे विषयी बक कागा। एहि सर निकट न जाहिँ अभागा॥
en: The very wicked and the slaves of pleasure, like cranes and crows, unlucky ones, do not come near this lake; for here there is no talk of sense pleasures, like snails, frogs and moss.

first: तेहि कारन आवत हिय हारे। कामी काक बलाक बिचारे॥
en: For this reason the poor lustful crows and cranes lose heart on the way here; coming to this lake is very hard, and no one can come without Rama's grace.

first: कठिन कुसङ्ग कुपन्थ कराला। तिन्ह के बचन बाघ हरि व्याला॥
en: Hard bad company is a terrible bad road, and the words of such people are tigers, lions and snakes on it; the many tangles of household work are huge mountains, very hard to cross,

first: बन बहु विषम मोह मद माना। नदी कुतर्क भयङ्कर नाना॥५॥
en: delusion, pride and vanity are many dense forests, and all kinds of false arguments are terrible rivers.

first: दो॰ – जे स्रद्धा सम्बल रहित, नहिँ सन्तन्ह कर साथ।
en: Those who have no provisions of faith, no company of saints, and to whom Raghunath is not dear, find this Manas very hard to reach.

first: चौ॰ – जौं करि कष्ट जाइ पुनि कोई। जातहि नीद जुड़ाई होई॥
en: And if someone does reach it after great trouble, as soon as he arrives he is seized by the fever-chill of sleep; the bitter cold of dullness grips his heart, and the unlucky man cannot bathe even though he is there.

first: करि न जाइ सर मज्जन पाना। फिरि आवइ समेत अभिमाना।
en: He cannot bathe in the lake or drink from it, and returns full of pride; and if anyone comes to ask him about it, he speaks ill of the lake to explain himself.

first: सकल विघ्न ब्यापहिँ नहिँ तेही। राम सुकृपा बिलोकहिं जेही॥
en: But none of these obstacles touch the one on whom Rama looks with kind eyes; he bathes in the lake with respect and is not burned by the three terrible kinds of suffering.

first: ते नर यह सर तजहिँ न काऊ। जिन्ह के राम चरन भल भाऊ॥
en: Those who have true love for Rama's feet never leave this lake. Brother, whoever wants to bathe in this lake should keep good company with all his heart.

first: अस मानस मानस चष चाही। भइ कबि बुद्धि बिमल अवगाही॥
en: Seeing such a Manas with the eye of the heart and diving into it, the poet's mind became pure; joy and eagerness rose in the heart, and a flood of love and delight poured out.

first: चली सुभग कबिता सरिता सी। राम बिमल जस जल भरिता सो॥
en: Fine poetry began to flow like a river, filled with the water of Rama's pure fame; its name is Sarayu, root of all blessing, and the views of the world and the Vedas are its two lovely banks.

first: नदी पुनीत सुमानस नन्दिनि। कलिमल त्रिन तरु मूल निकन्दिनि॥७॥
en: This holy river, daughter of the fine Manas lake, roots out the grass and trees of the sins of the age.

first: दो॰ – स्रोता त्रिविधि समाज पुर, ग्राम नगर दुहुँ कूल।
en: The three kinds of listeners are the towns, villages and cities on its two banks; the matchless gathering of saints is Ayodhya, root of all blessings.

first: चौ॰ – रामभगति सुरसरितहि जाई। मिली सुकीरति सरजु सुहाई॥
en: This lovely Sarayu of fine fame flowed on and joined the Ganga of devotion to Rama; the great river Son, the holy fame of Rama and his brother in battle, joined it too.

first: जुग घिच भगति देव धुनि धारा। सोहति सहित सुधिरति बिचारा॥
en: Between the two, the heavenly stream of devotion shines along with detachment and thought; this meeting of three rivers, which scares away the three kinds of suffering, flows on toward the ocean of Rama's true form.

first: मानस-मूल मिली सुरसरिही। सुनत सुजन-मन पावन करिही॥
en: With its source in the Manas, it has joined the Ganga and will purify the minds of good people who hear it; the wonderful episodes here and there are like the woods and gardens along the banks.

first: उमा-महेस-बिबाह बराती। ते जलचर अगनित बहु भाँती॥
en: The wedding guests at the marriage of Uma and Mahesh are its countless water creatures of many kinds; the joy and songs at Raghubar's birth are its lovely whirlpools and waves.

first: दो॰ – बालचरित चहुँ बन्धु के, बनज बिपुल बहु रङ्ग।
en: The childhood deeds of the four brothers are its many lotuses of many colours; the merits of the king, queens and family are the bees and water birds.

first: चौ॰ – सीय-स्वयम्बर-कथा सुहाई। सरित सुहावनि सो छबि छाई॥
en: The lovely story of Sita's bridegroom choice is the beauty spread over the river; the many clever questions are its boats, and the wise answers are the skilled boatmen.

first: सुनि अनुकथन परसपर होई। पथिक-समाज सोह सरि सोई॥
en: The talk among people after hearing is the crowd of travellers on the bank; the anger of Parashuram is the fierce current, and Rama's fine words are the well-built ghats.

first: सानुज राम-बिबाह-उछाहू। सो सुन उमग सुखद सब काहू॥
en: The joy of Rama's wedding with his brothers is the happy rising of the river that pleases all; those who are glad and thrilled to tell and hear it are the good people bathing joyfully.

first: राम तिलक हित मङ्गल साजा। परब जोग जनु जुरेउ समाजा॥
en: The festive preparations for Rama's crowning are like the crowd gathered for a holy bathing day; Kaikeyi's evil thought is the moss, from which came heavy troubles.

first: दो॰ – समन अमित उतपात सब, भरत चरित जप जाग।
en: Bharat's story is the prayer and sacrifice that calm all the endless troubles; the telling of the sins of the age and the faults of the wicked are the dirt, cranes and crows in the water.

first: चौ॰ – कीरति सरित छहूँ रितु रूरी। समय सुहावनि पावनि भूरी॥
en: This river of fame is fine in all six seasons, lovely and very holy at all times; the marriage of Shiva and the daughter of the Snow Mountain is early winter, and the joy of the Lord's birth is the pleasant late winter.

first: बरनब राम विवाह समाजू। सो मुद-मङ्गल मय रितुराजू॥
en: The account of Rama's wedding festivities I will give is spring, king of seasons, full of joy and blessing; Rama's going to the forest is the hard summer, and the story of the journey is its scorching sun and hot wind.

first: बरषा घोर निसाचर रारी। सुर-कुल-सालि सुमङ्गल-कारी॥
en: The fierce war with the demons is the rainy season, a blessing for the rice crop of the gods; the joy of Rama's reign, his humility and greatness, is the clear and pleasant autumn.

first: सती-सिरोमनि सिय-गुन-गाथा। सोइ गुन अमल अनूपम पाथा॥
en: The tale of the virtues of Sita, crown of faithful wives, is the pure and matchless quality of this water; Bharat's nature, always the same and beyond words, is its fine coolness.

first: दो॰ – अवलोकनि बोलनि मिलनि, प्रीति परसपर हास।
en: The glances, talk, meetings, love and laughter among the four brothers, and their fine brotherhood, are the sweetness and fragrance of the water.

first: चौ॰ – आरति बिनय दीनता मोरी। लघुता ललित सुबारि न खोरी॥
en: My pleading, prayers and humility are the lightness of this clear water, which is no fault in it; this wonderful water does good just by being heard, and removes the thirst of desire and the dirt of the mind.

first: राम सुप्रेमहि पोषत पानी। हरत सकल कलि-कलुष गलानी॥
en: This water nourishes true love for Rama and takes away all the sin and shame of the age; it dries up the weariness of worldly life, satisfies even satisfaction, and ends sin, sorrow, poverty and fault.

first: काम कोह मद मोह नसावन। बिमल बिबेक बिराग बढ़ावन॥
en: It destroys lust, anger, pride and delusion, and increases pure wisdom and detachment; by bathing in it and drinking it with respect, sin and pain will vanish from the heart.

first: जिन्ह एहि बारि न मानस धोये। ते कायर कलिकाल बिगोये॥
en: Those who have not washed their minds in this water are cowards ruined by the Kali age; like thirsty deer chasing a mirage made by the sun's rays, such beings will wander in misery.

first: दो॰ – मति अनुहारि लुबारि गुन, गन गनि मन अन्हवाइ।
en: Having counted the virtues of this fine water as far as his mind allows, and bathed his mind in it, and remembering Bhavani and Shankar, the poet tells the lovely story.

first: अब रघुपति-पद-पङ्करुह, हिय धरि पाइ प्रसाद।
en: Now, holding Raghupati's lotus feet in my heart and receiving his grace, I tell the lovely talk of the two great sages when they met.

first: चौ॰ – भरद्वाज मुनि बसहिँ प्रयागा। तिन्हहिँ राम-पद अति अनुरागा॥
en: The sage Bharadvaj lives at Prayag and has great love for Rama's feet; he is an ascetic, a store of calm, self-control and kindness, and very wise in the path to the highest goal.

first: माघ मकर-गत-रबि जब हाई। तीरथपतिहि आव सब कोई॥
en: In the month of Magh, when the sun enters Capricorn, everyone comes to the king of holy places; crowds of gods, demons, Kinnaras and men all bathe with reverence at the meeting of the three rivers.

first: पूजहिँ माधव-पद-जलजाता। परसि अषयवट हरषहिँ गाता॥
en: They worship the lotus feet of Madhava and are thrilled to touch the undying banyan tree. The hermitage of Bharadvaj is very holy, most lovely, and dear to the hearts of great sages.

first: तहाँ होइ मुनि-रिषय-समाजा। जाहिँ जे मज्जन तीरथराजा॥
en: There gather the sages and seers who come to bathe at the king of holy places; they bathe at dawn with joy and tell one another the tales of Hari's virtues.

first: दो॰ – ब्रह्म निरूपन धर्म-बिधि, बरनहिं तत्व-विभाग।
en: They discuss Brahman, the rules of duty and the divisions of truth, and speak of devotion to the Lord joined with knowledge and detachment.

first: चौ॰ – एहि प्रकार भरिभाघ नहाहीँ। पुनि सब निज निज आस्रम जाहीँ॥
en: In this way they bathe for the whole month of Magh and then all go back to their own hermitages; every year there is great joy, and after the Capricorn bathing the sages depart.

first: एक बार भरि मकर नहाये। सब मुनीस आस्रमन्ह सिधाये॥
en: Once, after the full Capricorn bathing, all the great sages left for their hermitages; but Bharadvaj held the feet of the very wise sage Yajnavalkya and kept him back.

first: सादर चरन-सरोज पखारे। अति पुनीत आसन बैठारे॥
en: With respect he washed his lotus feet and seated him on a very pure seat; after worshipping him and praising his fame, he spoke in very pure and gentle words:

first: नाथ एक संसय बड़ मोरे। करगत वेद-तत्त्व सब तोरे॥
en: 'Lord, I have one great doubt, and all the truth of the Vedas is in your hands; I feel fear and shame to say it, but if I do not, great harm will come.'

first: दो॰ – सन्त कहहिँ अस नीति प्रभु, स्रुति-पुरान-मुनि गाव।
en: 'Lord, the saints teach, and the Vedas, Puranas and sages sing, that pure wisdom does not come to the heart if one hides anything from one's teacher.'

first: चौ॰ – असबिचारि प्रगदउँ निजमोहू। हरहु नाथ करि जन पर छोहू॥
en: 'Thinking this, I show you my confusion; Lord, be kind to your servant and remove it. The saints, Puranas and Upanishads sing the boundless power of Rama's name.'

first: सन्तत जपत सम्भु अबिनासी। सिव भगवान ज्ञान-गुन-रासी॥
en: 'Shambhu, the undying, Lord Shiva, store of wisdom and virtue, repeats it all the time; of the four kinds of beings in the world, all who die in Kashi gain the highest state.'

first: सोपि राम-महिमा मुनिराया। सिव उपदेस करत करि दाया॥
en: 'That too, king of sages, is the glory of Rama, for Shiva in his kindness teaches it to them. I ask you, Lord, who is this Rama? Ocean of mercy, explain it to me.'

first: एक राम अवधेस-कुमारा। तिन्ह कर चरित बिदित संसारा॥
en: 'One Rama is the son of the king of Ayodhya, and his story is known in the world; he suffered greatly when parted from his wife, and in anger killed Ravana in battle.'

first: दो॰ – प्रभु सोइ राम कि अपर कोउ, जाहि जपत त्रिपुरारि।
en: 'Lord, is it that same Rama whom the enemy of Tripura repeats, or someone else? You are the home of truth and know all; think with wisdom and tell me.'

first: चौ॰ – जैसे मिटइ मोह भ्रम भारी। कहहु सो कथा नाथ बिस्तारी॥
en: 'Lord, tell me that story in full, so that my great delusion and confusion may go.' Yajnavalkya smiled and said, 'You know Raghupati's greatness well.'

first: रामभगत तुम्ह मन क्रम बानी। चतुराई तुम्हारि मैं जानी॥
en: 'You are Rama's devotee in mind, deed and word, and I know your cleverness; you want to hear the hidden virtues of Rama, so you ask as if you knew nothing.'

first: तात सुनहु सादर मन लाई। कहउँ राम कै कथा सुहाई॥
en: 'Dear one, listen with respect and attention; I will tell you the lovely story of Rama. Great delusion is the huge buffalo demon, and Rama's story is the terrible goddess Kali.'

first: रामकथा ससि-किरन समाना। सन्त चकोर करहिं जेहि पाना॥
en: 'Rama's story is like the moon's rays, which the chakor-like saints drink. Bhavani had just such a doubt, and then Mahadev explained it in full.'

first: दो॰ – कहउँ सो मति अनुहारि अब, उमा-सम्भु सम्बाद।
en: 'Now I tell, as my mind allows, the talk of Uma and Shambhu, when and why it took place; listen, sage, and your sorrow will go.'

first: चौ॰ – एक बार त्रेताजुग माहीं। सम्भु गये कुम्भज रिषि पाहीं॥
en: Once in the Treta age Shambhu went to the sage Agastya, with Sati, Bhavani, mother of the world; the sage worshipped him, knowing him as Lord of all.

first: रामकथा मुनिबर्ज बखानी। सुनी महेस परम सुख मानी॥
en: The great sage told Rama's story, and Mahesh heard it with great joy; the sage asked about lovely devotion to Hari, and Shambhu, finding him fit, explained it.

first: कहत सुनत रघुपति-गुन-गाथा। कछु दिन तहाँ रहे गिरिनाथा॥
en: Telling and hearing the tale of Raghupati's virtues, the lord of the mountain stayed there some days; then taking leave of the sage, the enemy of Tripura set off home with Daksha's daughter.

first: तेहि अवसर भञ्जन महिभारा। हरि रघुबंस लीन्ह अवतारा॥
en: At that time, to remove the earth's burden, Hari had taken birth in Raghu's line; obeying his father, giving up the kingdom and living as a hermit, the undying Lord was roaming the Dandaka forest.

first: दो॰ – हृदय विचारत जात हर, केहि बिधि दरसन होइ।
en: As he went, Hara thought in his heart, 'How can I see him? The Lord has come down in hidden form; if I go to him, everyone will know.'

first: सो॰ – सङ्कर उर अतिछाभ, सती न जानइ मरम सोइ।
en: There was great turmoil in Shankar's heart, but Sati did not know the secret. Tulsi says: his mind was afraid, but his eyes were greedy for the sight.

first: चौ॰ – रावन मरन मनुज कर जाँचा। प्रभु बिधि बचन कीन्ह चह साँचा॥
en: 'Ravana asked to die at the hands of a man, and the Lord wants to make Brahma's word true; if I do not go, I will always regret it.' He thought hard but could find no way.

first: एहि बिधि भये सोचबस ईसा। तेही समय जाइ दससीसा॥
en: While the Lord Shiva was caught in this worry, just then the ten-headed Ravana went and took the low Marich with him, who at once became a false deer.

first: करि छल मूढ़ हरी बैदेही। प्रभु प्रमाउ तस बिदित न तेही॥
en: By trickery the fool carried off Vaidehi, not knowing the Lord's true power. After killing the deer the Lord came back with his brother, and seeing the empty hermitage his eyes filled with tears.

first: बिरह बिकल नर इव रघुराई। खोजत बिपिन फिरत दोउ भाई॥
en: Like a man distressed by separation, Raghurai and his brother wandered through the forest searching; he who never knows union or parting was seen plainly in unbearable grief.

first: दो॰ – अति बिचित्र रघुपति चरित, जानहिँ परम सुजान।
en: Raghupati's ways are very wonderful, and only the truly wise know them; the dull-minded, under the sway of delusion, think something else in their hearts.

first: चौ॰ – सम्भु समय तेहि रामहिँ देखा। उपजा हिय अति हरष बिसेखा॥
en: At that time Shambhu saw Rama, and great and special joy rose in his heart; he gazed his fill at that ocean of beauty, but knowing the time was wrong, he did not make himself known.

first: जय सच्चिदानन्द जग-पावन। अस कहि चलेउ मनोज-नसावन॥
en: 'Victory to the Being-Awareness-Bliss who purifies the world,' said the destroyer of Kama, and went on; as Shiva walked on with Sati, the store of kindness thrilled with joy again and again.

first: सती सो दसा सम्भु कै देखी। उर उपजा सन्देह बिसेखी॥
en: Sati saw Shambhu in that state, and a great doubt rose in her heart: 'Shankar is the Lord of the world and its friend; gods, men and sages all bow their heads to him.'

first: तिन्ह नृप-सुतहि कीन्ह परनामा। कहि सच्चिदानन्द परधामा।
en: 'Yet he bowed to a king's son, calling him Being-Awareness-Bliss, the highest abode; he was lost in joy seeing his beauty, and even now the love in his heart cannot be held back.'

first: दो॰ – ब्रह्म जो ब्यापक बिरज अज, अकल अनीह अभेद।
en: 'Brahman is all-pervading, pure, unborn, without parts, without desire and without difference, whom even the Vedas do not know; can he take a body and become a man?'

first: चौ॰ – बिनु जो सुर-हित नर-तनु-धारी। सोउ सरबज्ञ जथा त्रिपुरारी॥
en: 'And Vishnu, who takes a human body for the good of the gods, is all-knowing like Shiva; would he, the home of wisdom, Lakshmi's lord and the enemy of demons, search for a woman like an ignorant man?'

first: सम्भु गिरा पुनि मृषा न होई। सिव सरबज्ञ जान सब कोई॥
en: 'Yet Shambhu's words can never be false; everyone knows Shiva is all-knowing.' Such endless doubt arose in her mind, and no understanding could reach her heart.

first: जद्यपि प्रगट न कहेउ भवानी। हर अन्तरजामी सब जानी॥
en: Though Bhavani did not say it aloud, Hara, who knows all hearts, knew everything. 'Listen, Sati,' he said, 'this is a woman's way; never keep such doubt in your heart.'

first: जासु कथा कुम्भज रिषि गाई। भगति जासु मैं मुनिहिँ सुनाई॥
en: 'He whose story the sage Agastya sang, and whose devotion I told the sage, is that same Raghubir, my chosen Lord, whom steady sages always serve.'

first: मुनिधीर जोगी सिद्ध सन्तत, बिमल मन जेहि ध्यावहीं।
en: 'He on whom steady sages, yogis and perfected ones always meditate with pure minds, whose fame the Vedas, Puranas and scriptures sing saying "not this", that same Rama, all-pervading Brahman, lord of all the worlds and master of maya, has come down by his own will, for his devotees, as the jewel of Raghu's line.'

first: सो॰ – लाग न उर उपदेस, जदपि कहेउ सिव बार बहु।
en: Though Shiva told her many times, the teaching did not go into her heart; then, knowing in his heart the power of Hari's maya, Mahesh smiled and spoke.

first: चौ॰ – जौँ तुम्हरे मन अति सन्देहू। तौ किन जाइ परीछा लेहू॥
en: 'If there is so much doubt in your mind, why not go and test him? I will sit in the shade of this banyan tree until you come back to me.'

first: जैसे जाइ मोह-भ्रम-भारी। करेहु सो जतन बिबेक बिचारी॥
en: 'Act with careful thought, so that your great delusion and confusion may go.' With Shiva's leave Sati went, thinking, 'What shall I do?'

first: इहाँ सम्भु अस मन अनुमाना। दच्छ-सुत्ता कहँ नहि कल्याना॥
en: Here Shambhu guessed in his mind: 'Daksha's daughter is heading for harm; when her doubts do not go even when I speak, fate is against her and no good will come.'

first: होइहि सोइ जो राम रचि राखा। को करि तरक बढ़ावइ साखा॥
en: 'What Rama has planned will happen; who would add more branches by arguing?' Saying this he began to repeat Hari's name, and Sati went to where the Lord, home of joy, was.

first: दो॰ – पुनि पुनि हृदय बिचार करि, धरि सीता कर रूप।
en: After thinking again and again, she took Sita's form and walked ahead on the path by which the king of men was coming.

first: चौ॰ – लछिमन दीख उमा-कृत-बेषा। चकित मये भ्रम हृदय बिसेषा॥
en: Lakshman saw the form Uma had taken and was amazed and greatly puzzled; but being very deep and steady of mind, and knowing the Lord's power, he could say nothing.

first: सती कपट जानेउ सुर-स्वामी। सबदरसी सबअन्तर-जामी॥
en: The Lord of the gods, who sees all and knows all hearts, saw through Sati's trick; he is the all-knowing Lord Rama, by remembering whom ignorance is removed.

first: सती कीन्ह चह तहउँ दुराऊ। देखहु नारि-सुभाउ-प्रभाऊ॥
en: Even there Sati wanted to hide the truth; see the power of a woman's nature! Praising the force of his own maya in his heart, Rama smiled and spoke softly.

first: जोरि पानि प्रभु कोन्ह प्रनामू। पिता समेत लीन्ह निज नामू॥
en: The Lord joined his hands and bowed, giving his own name and his father's; then he asked, 'Where is Shiva? Why are you wandering in the forest alone?'

first: दो॰ – राम-बचन-मृदु गूढ़ सुनि, उपजा अति सङ्कोच।
en: Hearing Rama's gentle but meaningful words, she felt great shame; Sati went back to Mahesh in fear, with a heavy worry in her heart.

first: चौ॰ – मैं सङ्कर कर कहा न माना। निज अज्ञान राम पर आना॥
en: 'I did not listen to Shankar and put my own ignorance on Rama; what answer will I give now?' A terrible burning rose in her heart.

first: जाना राम सती दुख पावा। निज प्रभाउ कछु प्रगटि जनावा॥
en: Rama knew Sati was in pain and showed her a little of his power. As she walked Sati saw a wonder: Rama was ahead on the path with Sita and his brother.

first: फिरि चितवा पाछे प्रभु देखा। सहित बन्धु सिय सुन्दर बेखा॥
en: She turned and looked back and saw the Lord with his brother and Sita in lovely dress; wherever she looked, there the Lord was seated, served by skilled perfected ones and great sages.

first: देखे सिव बिधि बिष्नु अनेका। अमित प्रभाउ एक तेँ एका॥
en: She saw many Shivas, Brahmas and Vishnus, each greater in power than the last; she saw all the gods in many forms bowing at the Lord's feet and serving him.

first: दो॰ – सती बिधात्री इन्दिरा, देखी अमित अनूप।
en: She saw countless matchless Satis, Saraswatis and Lakshmis, each in a form to match the form of Brahma or the other god she was with.

first: चौ॰ – देखे जहँ तहँ रघुपति जेते। सक्तिन्ह सहित सकल सुर तेते॥
en: Wherever she saw a Raghupati, she saw just as many gods with their consorts; and she saw all the moving and unmoving beings of the world in many forms.

first: पूजहिं प्रभुहि देव बहु बेखा। राम-रूप दूसर नहिँ देखा॥
en: The gods worshipped the Lord in many forms, but she saw no second form of Rama; she saw many Raghupatis with Sita, but their forms were not many, always the same.

first: सोइ रघुबर सोइ लछिमन सीता। देखि सती अति भई सभीता॥
en: Seeing the same Raghubar, the same Lakshman and Sita, Sati was terrified; her heart shook, she lost all sense of her body, and she sat down on the path with closed eyes.

first: बहुरि बिलोकेउ नयन उधारी। कछु न दीख तहँ दच्छकुमारी॥
en: When Daksha's daughter opened her eyes and looked again, she saw nothing there; bowing her head again and again at Rama's feet, she went to where the lord of the mountain was.

first: दो॰ – गई समीप महेस तब, हँसि पूछी कुसलात।
en: When she came near, Mahesh smiled and asked how she was: 'Tell me the whole truth, how did you test him?'

first: चौ॰ – सती समुझि रघुबीर प्रभाऊ। भय-बस प्रभु सन कीन्ह दुराऊ॥
en: Understanding Raghubir's power, Sati in fear hid the truth from her lord: 'Master, I did not test him at all; I only bowed to him as you did.'

first: जो तुम्ह कहा सो मृषा न होई। मोरे मन प्रतीति अति सोई॥
en: 'What you said can never be false; my mind fully trusts it.' Then Shankar looked by meditation and came to know all that Sati had done.

first: बहुरि राम-मायहि सिर नावा। प्रेरि सतिहि जेहि झूठ कहावा॥
en: Then he bowed his head to Rama's maya, which had moved Sati to tell a lie; wise Shambhu thought in his heart, 'Hari's will, which is fate, is mighty.'

first: सती कीन्ह सीता कर वेषा। सिव-उर भयउ बिषाद बिसेषा॥
en: Sati had taken Sita's form, and Shiva felt great sorrow at heart: 'If I now love Sati as my wife, the path of devotion is broken and it would be wrong.'

first: दो॰ – परम-प्रेम तजि जाइ नहिँ, किये प्रेम बड़ पाप।
en: His great love could not be given up, and to keep loving her as a wife would be a great sin; Mahesh said nothing openly, but his heart was in deep pain.

first: चौ॰ – तब सङ्कर प्रमु-पद सिर नावा। सुमिरत राम हृदय अस आवा॥
en: Then Shankar bowed his head at the Lord's feet, and as he remembered Rama this came to his heart: 'In this body Sati and I will not meet as wife and husband'; Shiva made this vow in his mind.

first: अस बिचारि सङ्कर मतिधीरा। चले भवन सुमिरत रघुबीरा॥
en: Thinking so, steady-minded Shankar set off home, remembering Raghubir; as he went, a lovely voice spoke from the sky: 'Victory to you, Mahesh, you have made your devotion firm.'

first: अस पन तुम्ह बिनु करइ को आना। राम भगत समरथ भगवाना॥
en: 'Who but you could make such a vow? You are Rama's devotee, mighty and divine.' Hearing the voice from the sky, Sati worried in her heart and shyly asked Shiva,

first: कीन्ह कवन पन कहहु कृपाला। सत्य-धाम प्रभु दीनदयाला॥
en: 'Kind lord, home of truth, friend of the humble, tell me what vow you have made.' Though Sati asked in many ways, the enemy of Tripura did not tell her.

first: दो॰ – सतीहृदय अनुमान किय, सब जानेउँ सरबज्ञ।
en: Sati guessed in her heart, 'The all-knowing one knows everything; I deceived Shambhu; a woman is by nature foolish and unknowing.'

first: सो॰ – जल पय सरिस बिकाइ, देखहु प्रीति कि रीति मलि।
en: See the fine way of love: water mixed with milk is sold as milk; but as soon as the sourness of deceit falls in, they separate and the taste is lost.

first: चौ॰ – हृदय सोच समुझत निज करनी। चिन्ता अमित जाइ नहिँ बरनी॥
en: Thinking of what she had done, she felt sorrow and endless worry beyond words; she knew that Shiva, the deep ocean of mercy, had not spoken of her fault openly.

first: सङ्कर-रुख अवलोकि भवानी। प्रभु मोहि तजेउ हृदय अंकुलानी॥
en: Seeing Shankar's manner, Bhavani grew restless at heart, feeling 'my lord has left me'; knowing her sin she could say nothing, and her heart burned like a potter's kiln.

first: सतिहि ससोच जानि बृषकेतू। कही कथा सुन्दर सुख-हेतू॥
en: Knowing Sati was full of sorrow, Shiva told her lovely stories to cheer her; telling many old tales along the way, the Lord of the world reached Kailash.

first: तहँ पुनि समुझि समुझि पन आपन। बइठे बट तर करि कमलासन॥
en: There, thinking again and again of his vow, he sat under the banyan tree in the lotus pose; Shankar returned to his own true nature and fell into deep, unbroken meditation.

first: दो॰ – सत्ती बसहि कैलास तब, अधिक सोच मन माहिँ।
en: Then Sati lived on Kailash with great sorrow in her mind; no one knew the secret at all, and each day passed for her like an age.
